grades.quote: Behind the scenes, the middleware encodes the procedure arguments into a request message and extracts the return value from the response message. Similarly, the server application code can take the form of an ordinary procedure. By the time it is invoked, the procedure arguments have already been extracted from the request message, freeing it from that responsibility.
grades.reason: Directly explains client-side argument encoding and result extraction, and server-side argument extraction before invocation.

grades.quote: Figure 10.4: In order for the server application code to be free from communication details, it can be a normal procedure invoked by a portion of the RPC runtime sometimes called a skeleton or a tie.
grades.reason: Explains stub argument packaging and result extraction, and identifies the skeleton as the runtime component invoking the server procedure.
